headline: China orders state agencies to uninstall its government-only Windows 10 edition
summary: Beijing accelerates planned retirement of the custom Windows build over data security concerns, boosting domestic OS vendors.
details: China's Ministry of State Security has reportedly instructed some state-linked organizations to remove a customized version of Windows 10 from their machines. This directive accelerates a planned retirement that was originally scheduled for February 2027.

The affected software is a government edition developed by C&M Information Technologies (CMIT), a joint venture between Microsoft and China Electronics Technology Group. This build is based on Windows 10 Enterprise but omits consumer-facing components like OneDrive and allows for in-country updates and activation.

Sources familiar with the matter attribute the order to data security concerns, though specific vulnerabilities have not been detailed. This move sent shares of Chinese OS vendors like Hunan Kylinsec and Archermind surging.

Microsoft stated it is unaware of any security incident affecting this product and that it continues to receive regular security updates. Mainstream support for Windows 10 globally ended in October 2025.

Sources familiar with the matter attribute the order to data security concerns, though specific vulnerabilities have not been detailed. This move sent shares of Chinese OS vendors like Hunan Kylinsec and Archermind surging.

Microsoft stated it is unaware of any security incident affecting this product and that it continues to receive regular security updates. Mainstream support for Windows 10 globally ended in October 2025.
